overview: This House resolution condemns the June 1, 2025, attack in Boulder, Colorado, in which a man threw Molotov cocktails at people peacefully marching for the release of hostages held by Hamas, injuring at least 14 people. It names the attacker, an Egyptian citizen who it says had overstayed a tourist visa after applying for asylum, and states that his case shows the need for stronger screening of visa applicants and removal of people who violate their visa terms. The resolution condemns the attack as antisemitic terrorism, says open communication between state and local police and federal agencies is key to preventing attacks, and thanks law enforcement, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The House adopted it on June 9, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution condemns an antisemitic attack while pointing to what they see as real gaps in visa screening and enforcement that the case exposed.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law, and that tying the condemnation to immigration enforcement turns a statement of support for victims into a debate over immigration policy.
